subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should extension-relay permanently expose instance-scoped opaque target IDs as the CDP identity, with stale IDs invalid across every relay restart, rather than retaining raw renderer target IDs or a temporary compatibility path?
rationale: This changes the externally observable CDP target-ID contract; source-level repairs can make IDs non-reusable, but maintainers must choose the intended compatibility and migration boundary.

options.title: Adopt nonce-scoped relay identities
options.body: Add a per-relay-instance nonce to public handles, document the intentional relay-CDP identity change, and prove stale IDs cannot address a new binding after restart.

options.title: Retain a temporary compatibility bridge
options.body: Keep a narrowly scoped migration path for raw renderer IDs while clients move to relay-owned handles, with an explicit removal plan.

recommendation.title: Adopt nonce-scoped relay identities
recommendation.body: Add a per-relay-instance nonce to public handles, document the intentional relay-CDP identity change, and prove stale IDs cannot address a new binding after restart.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical issue specifies the desired relay identity lifecycle and the PR asks this person to confirm the public contract.
